opportunities.title: Synthesis Grants

amount.raw: Up to £30,000 over two years for groups of 8-15 participants

opportunities.eligibility_summary: Main applicant must have BES membership; working groups of 8-15 individuals with a diverse mix of career stages, institutions (not solely academic), genders and backgrounds; international participation; EDI and FAIR principles required.
opportunities.summary: Funds new two-year synthesis groups that bring together interdisciplinary groups of 8-15 individuals to analyse and synthesise existing data, fostering collaboration and mentoring, with outputs informing decision-makers. Groups meet via hybrid model with two in-person meetings.

opportunities.title: Long-term Research Grants

amount.raw: £500 per year for a decade (up to £3,500 claimable in year 1 covering the first five years, plus a further £3,500 in year 6)

opportunities.eligibility_summary: Must have BES membership; open to all types of ecologists including conservation practitioners (e.g. reserve managers, consultants) and university academics; awarded to individuals, not organisations.
opportunities.summary: Provides a small amount of funding each year for 10 years to enable existing short-term projects with 1-2 years of data to be funded into the long term, funding annual data collection (ecological restoration, habitat creation, alien species control, climate change) anywhere in the world.

opportunities.title: Pedagogical Research and Development Grants
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Must have BES membership; open to anyone involved in teaching ecology at any level (early years to lifelong learning, formal or informal settings); no geographical restrictions; awarded to individuals, not organisations; projects maximum 12 months.
opportunities.summary: Funds research informing teaching and learning practices in ecology, providing up to £5,000 for evidence-based learning projects that improve learners' experience and promote excellence in teaching.

opportunities.title: Connecting Ecologists with Other Disciplines Grants
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Must have BES membership; open to PhD students, postdoctoral fellows, early career ecologists, established researchers or employees of other organisations; undergraduates and masters students not eligible; must have employer/supervisor approval and a willing host organisation; placements up to 12 months.
opportunities.summary: Promotes interdisciplinary skills by funding up to £20,000 towards placements that immerse an ecologist in another professional world (another discipline, NGO/charity, public sector organisation, business) where ecology can make a difference.

opportunities.title: Small Research Grants
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Researchers from all countries globally; projects can be conducted anywhere in the world; will not cover principal researcher salary, bench fees or vehicle hire; not a scholarship and cannot fund degree/masters completion or funded fellowships.
opportunities.summary: Provides up to £5,000 for new and innovative ecological research of the highest international standard, supporting work that advances ecological science.

opportunities.title: Outreach and Engagement Grants

amount.raw: Up to £2,000 (may be used as part-funding for larger projects)

opportunities.eligibility_summary: Lead applicant must have BES membership; open to individuals, teams and organisations across all experience levels; no restrictions on where applicants come from or carry out work; projects maximum 12 months and aimed at non-academic audiences.
opportunities.summary: Provides up to £2,000 for individuals, teams and organisations to deliver independent outreach, public engagement and science communication activities that engage public audiences with the excitement, importance and relevance of ecological science.

opportunities.title: Training and Travel Grants

amount.raw: A maximum of £500 for in-person events; £250 for virtual conferences/courses

opportunities.eligibility_summary: Must be a BES member; must be a PhD student or postgraduate researcher (postdocs, undergraduates and masters students not eligible); must work/study at a university or research institution; must work in ecological science within the BES remit; must give a presentation if attending a meeting.
opportunities.summary: Helps PhD students and postgraduate researchers meet the costs of specialist field training courses and travel costs associated with presenting their work at workshops and conferences. Awarded on a lottery-based system.

opportunities.title: Annual Meeting Grants 2026
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Must be a BES member at any career stage; must be a citizen of and based in the Global South; must be travelling from and returning to the Global South country; must have applied to present at the Annual Meeting; must be at least three years since last BES Training and Travel Grant.
opportunities.summary: Supports researchers based in Global South countries to attend the BES Annual Meeting in the UK, covering travel to/from the UK and related costs (registration, transport, food, accommodation) up to £1,000. Awards via a lottery-based system.
